answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The lantern multiplier is published, charged in yarrow, and vertex lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2096 identities would post 3817 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
